candidates.old:
INC pixel_table_address_high    \ Use white pixel table for most enemies
.pm_not_white_g0b1b
    AND #&7F                        \ A = mover type
    STA &7A
    TAX
    JSR check_if_mover_is_on_screen \ Returns carry set if mover not on screen
    BCS not_white + 4
    JSR get_mover_sprite_and_screen_addresses
    JSR plot_mover_sprite           \ Plot first part of mover (e.g. player's legs)
    LDY mover
    LDA movers_x_low,Y              \ get_mover_Y_x without &C5: still movers_x_high,Y from the first
candidates.new:
INC pixel_table_address_high    \ Use white pixel table for most enemies
IF GAMEPLAY_ANY = 0
    BRA pm_not_white_g0b1b
    SKIP 0
ENDIF
.pm_not_white_g0b1b
    AND #&7F                        \ A = mover type
    STA &7A
    TAX
    JSR check_if_mover_is_on_screen \ Returns carry set if mover not on screen
    BCS not_white + 4
    JSR get_mover_sprite_and_screen_addresses
    JSR plot_mover_sprite           \ Plot first part of mover (e.g. player's legs)
    LDA movers_x_low,Y              \ get_mover_Y_x without &C5: still movers_x_high,Y from the first
candidates.summary: plot_mover: the LDY mover after the first plot_mover_sprite is dead: JSR plot_mover_sprite -> JSR walk_column, which starts with LDY mover and never writes Y again (no JSR inside, every path ends at .walked RTS), and plot_mover_sprite's tail (LDA #&40 / STA / RTS) leaves Y alone, so Y = mover already and LDA movers_x_low,Y can follow the JSR directly (3 cycles, 2 bytes, on-screen movers only: 1.97 a pass). The 2 bytes saved are given back as a cold-path pad (IF GAMEPLAY_ANY = 0: BRA pm_not_white_g0b1b + SKIP 0 after the white-table INC, which runs 0.1 times a pass) so every later address, page crossing and the um_next / move_mover_* ASSERTs stay exactly as they are. Measured on scratch builds of HEAD ff62e12 (DEBUG_LIVES, pcprof work a pass, --unclobber): seed 1 (600 passes) 31325.4 -> 31319.8 (-5.6), RIGHT (300 passes from 50) 38610.2 -> 38606.0 (-4.2); passlock 3000 passes seed 1 --screen: state and screen identical. Without the pad (-2 bytes) the same build measured -0.7 / +0.9 (a BPL cell and a BPL move_mover_x_done start crossing a page), so do not drop the pad. I also built and measured inlining plot_mover_sprite (and walk_column) into plot_mover's first call (-12 cycles a call, -35..-50 a pass) but it needs +16..+107 bytes, the DEBUG_FULLREDRAW twin has 4 bytes of room (+57 overran by 53) and +9..+17 breaks the um_next ASSERT, so it is not offered.
candidates.equivalence: Original: JSR plot_mover_sprite; LDY mover; LDA movers_x_low,Y. New: JSR plot_mover_sprite; LDA movers_x_low,Y. walk_column (the only code plot_mover_sprite runs between its STAs and its RTS that could touch Y) begins LDY mover, has no other write to Y (no LDY/TAY/INY/DEY/STY/PLY, no JSR, no stack ops) and all its exits reach .walked: RTS; plot_mover_sprite then does LDA #&40 / STA pixel_table_address_low / RTS. So on return Y = mover (zero page &79, which nothing in between writes), the same value LDY mover would load. LDY's N/Z are overwritten by the LDA that follows; C and V are untouched by either; A, X unchanged by LDY. Every entry to the changed code is the fall-through from the JSR (no label inside); exits unchanged. The pad: after INC pixel_table_address_high (the white-table path), BRA pm_not_white_g0b1b with SKIP 0 jumps to the next instruction: only 3 extra cycles on that cold path, no register or flag the path reads is affected (the next instruction AND #&7F sets N/Z, A and C unchanged by BRA); the branches to .pm_not_white_g0b1b (BPL, BCS, BEQ x2) still land on the same instruction. Gameplay builds (no pad): same code minus the 2 bytes, no later alignment dependency, assembled OK.
candidates.relies_on: walk_column and plot_mover_sprite leaving Y = mover (zero page &79) on exit; another candidate that changes walk_column's Y at its RTS (or adds a Y write to plot_mover_sprite) would invalidate this. Page crossings: none moved (only .pm_not_white_g0b1b itself moves, +2, inside plot_mover: its taken BPL/BCS/BEQ stay on page &1A), the bench/ship/full/release builds keep every address from plot_mover_sprite on identical to HEAD (pad = the 2 bytes saved; checked by building HEAD and the candidate: same labels). Both game .6502 bank layouts untouched. If another kept candidate changes the bytes of plot_mover's region before this one, the pad should be re-chosen (it must equal the bytes saved to keep later addresses; a 2-byte pad is BRA + SKIP 0). Assembles in DEBUG_LIVES, DEBUG_LIVES+DEBUG_FULLREDRAW, plain, -Release, GAMEPLAY_SHIELD, all GAMEPLAY_*, SKY_HELI=0. The pad's BRA is a 65C02 opcode already used throughout the file.
